title: Immunofluorescence microscopy-based detection of ssDNA foci by BrdU in mammalian cells
protocol: Detach T24 cells from maintenance culture flasks using Trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) by incubating flasks for a few minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Pre-warm cell culture medium and Trypsin-EDTA solution to avoid excessive thermal shifts in cells.
Check whether cell morphology appears normal before starting any treatments, and ensure there is no contamination present in the wells.
Sterilize forceps and coverslips before using them for cell culture.
Neutralize trypsin by adding at least 2 volumes of complete media (McCoy’s 5A Medium with 10% FBS).
Collect cells into a Falcon tube of appropriate size.
Centrifuge cells at 900–1,000 × g at 20°C–22°C for 3–4 min.
Gently aspirate media so as not to disturb the cell pellet.
Resuspend cell pellets in complete culture medium.
Seed cells into 6-well plates so they are around 50%–60% confluent the next day.
Count cells in trypan blue solution (1:1 ratio of cells and trypan blue reagent) using a standard or automated hemocytometer.
Add sterilized round cover glasses (9 mm; thickness No.1) to the bottom of the wells with fresh media in it.
Gently press down with forceps to make sure that the cover glasses stick to the bottom of the wells.
Add cell suspension to the wells, making the total volume 2 mL.
The next day, add 10 μM BrdU to 50%–60% confluent cells and keep for 24 hours.

When using other chemicals/inhibitors to study their effects on ssDNA generation, add these to the media with BrdU in the last few hours of the 24-hour BrdU treatment at a concentration needed according to your specific compound.
For example, add HU (500 μM) for 1 hour before sample processing.
Add 10 μM EdU to cells recovered with culture media containing BrdU in the last 20 minutes prior to cell fixation to mark cells in S phase.
Irradiate cells with 2 Gy IR.
Maintain non-irradiated cells in a separate 6-well plate as an internal control.
Incubate control and irradiated cells in complete media at 37°C and 5% CO2 for the desired amount of time prior to fixing and processing for IF.
Transfer coverslips into individual wells in a 12-well plate and wash the media off with 1 mL ice-cold PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add 1 mL of ice-cold pre-extraction buffer for 5 min over ice.
Aspirate pre-extraction buffer and wash once with 1 mL cold 1× PBS to remove pre-extraction buffer.
Add 1 mL of freshly prepared ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to each well.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL 1× PBS at 20°C–22°C for 2–3 min each.
Add 1 mL of 5% BSA in PBS and incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Prepare Click-iT reaction mixture according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add 30 μL droplets of Click-iT reaction solution on a parafilm in a wet chamber.
Lift coverslips from the 12-well plate with forceps.
Dry extra liquid on a tissue paper.
Place coverslips upside down on the Click-iT reaction buffer.
Incubate for 30 min in the dark.
Transfer coverslips back to the 12-well plate.
Wash cells twice for 2–3 min.
Keep coverslips in the blocking solution at 4°C overnight or up to a few days if necessary.
Cover plates with aluminum foil during washes.
Dilute primary BrdU antibody in 2.5% BSA/PBS solution (BrdU antibody concentration: 1:300).
Ensure the coverslip is fully covered in antibody solution.
Add 30 μL droplets of antibody solution on parafilm in a wet chamber.
Lift coverslips from the 12-well plate with forceps, dry extra liquid on a tissue paper and place upside down on the antibody droplet.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Transfer the coverslips back to the 12-well plate, fixed cells facing up.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS at 20°C–22°C into each well for 5 min.
Gently remove PBS by using a vacuum pump.
Repeat this step 2 additional times (washing step; a total of 3 washing steps).
Dilute secondary fluorescent antibody (Alexa Fluor 488) in antibody dilution buffer.
Add 30 μL droplets of antibody solution on parafilm in a wet chamber.
Lift coverslips from the 12-well plate using forceps as before, dry extra liquid and place upside down on antibody droplets.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Transfer the coverslips back to 12-well plate with fixed cells facing up.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS at 20°C–22°C into each well for 5 min.
Gently remove PBS by using a vacuum pump.
Repeat this step 2 additional times (washing step; a total of 3 washing steps).
Dilute Cyclin A antibody in 2.5% BSA/PBS solution (Cyclin A antibody concentration: 1:500).
Add 30 μL droplets of diluted Cyclin A antibody on parafilm in a wet chamber.
Lift coverslips from the 12-well plate using forceps, dry extra liquid and place upside down on antibody droplets.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Transfer the coverslips back to 12-well plate with fixed cells facing up.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS at 20°C–22°C into each well for 5 min.
Gently remove PBS by using a vacuum pump.
Repeat this step 2 additional times (washing step; a total of 3 washing steps).
Dilute secondary fluorescent antibody (Alexa Fluor 594) in antibody dilution buffer.
Add 30 μL droplets of diluted Alexa Fluor 594 on parafilm in a wet chamber.
Lift coverslips from the 12-well plate using forceps, dry extra liquid and place upside down on antibody droplets.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Transfer the coverslips back to 12-well plate with fixed cells facing up.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS at 20°C–22°C into each well for 5 min.
Gently remove PBS by using a vacuum pump.
Repeat this step 2 additional times (washing step; a total of 3 washing steps).
Use ProLong Diamond antifade with DAPI mounting solution to make individual droplets on microscopy slides.
Mount the coverslips over the droplets (one droplet for each coverslip).
Avoid bubbles when applying the mounting solution on microscopy slides to ensure imaging quality.
Add the mounting droplets just before placing the coverslips to prevent hardening of the solution.
Incubate cells in DAPI with PBS at a final concentration of 1 μg/mL for 10 minutes in the dark as an alternative staining method.
Wash cells once with 1× PBS for 5 minutes after DAPI incubation.
Stain nuclei with Hoechst 33342 dye in PBS at a final concentration of 5 μg/mL for 10 minutes at 20°C–22°C in the dark as an alternative to DAPI.
Mount stained cells using ProLong Glass Antifade Mountant after nuclear staining with Hoechst 33342.
Dip coverslips gently in ddH2O to remove salts.
Dry extra liquid on kimwipes.
Dry extra liquid superficially and quickly on coverslips to avoid excessive dilution of the mounting medium.
Place coverslips sample-upper side down (fixed cells facing the mounting solution).
Incubate at 20°C–22°C in the dark for 30 min minimum.
Store mounted slides at 4°C in the dark after incubation.
Capture images using an epifluorescent or confocal microscope using the DAPI channel with a 10× lens to locate cells.
Change magnification to either 40× or 63× oil lens and capture images with DAPI, FITC, and TRITC channels.
Adjust laser power and gain without overexposing samples even in the brightest condition.
